question.problem:
$$
\{\begin{aligned}a+\frac{3}{5}b=\frac{9}{5} \\ \frac{3}{7}a+\frac{1}{7}b=1\end{aligned}
$$

Find the solution to the system of equations given above.
question.worked_solution:
To get rid of fractions, we multiply the first equation by $5$ and the second equation by $7,$ as follows:

$$
\{\begin{aligned}a+\frac{3}{5}b=\frac{9}{5} & |\times 5 \\ \frac{3}{7}a+\frac{1}{7}b=1 & |\times 7\end{aligned}\,⟹\,\{\begin{aligned}5a+3b=9 \\ 3a+b=7\end{aligned}
$$

We will use the substitution method to solve the system. Notice that the second equation can easily be solved for $b:$

$$
\begin{aligned}3a+b & =7 \\ b & =7-3a\end{aligned}
$$

We substitute $b=7-3a$ into the first equation and then solve for $a:$

$$
\begin{aligned}5a+3b & =9 \\ 5a+3(7-3a) & =9 \\ 5a+21-9a & =9 \\ -4a & =-12 \\ a & =3\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, to find the value of $b,$ we substitute $a=3$ into the equation $b=7-3a$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}b & =7-3a \\  & =7-3(3) \\  & =7-9 \\  & =-2\end{aligned}
$$

Thus, the solution to the system of equations is $a=3$ and $b=-2.$
